The Great Coding Reset: How AI Is Changing Software Engineering

There's been endless discussion about AI changing the workplace. One job has felt it to the core: software engineering. We set out to understand exactly how deeply the tools have reshaped the daily work of writing code.

Interviews with two dozen engineers reveal a craft in flux. Autocomplete became autopilot; review became the bottleneck; and the definition of a "senior" engineer quietly shifted toward judgment over keystrokes.

What follows is a field guide to the new normal, assembled from those conversations and the artifacts they shared — pull requests, prompts, and post-mortems from a year of building with machines that write.

The throughline: the work did not disappear. It moved. And the engineers who thrived were the ones who moved with it, treating the model as a fast, tireless, occasionally-wrong collaborator rather than a replacement.
